title: One Intervention per Component is Enough: Towards Identifiability in Linear Stochastic Dynamics from Steady State
claim: Estimation error falls as interventions increase, and joint mean-plus-covariance fitting beats covariance-only fitting, with graphical conditions holding more often as interventions grow.
layout: 4 line plots in a row, shared x-axis of interventions, error bars
description: A single row of four line plots with panel labels beneath each. Panels (a), (b) and (c) are labeled with the parameters Λ, D and b. Each plots relative error on the y-axis against the number of interventions (0 to 10) on the x-axis. Blue curves show the mean-plus-covariance estimator and orange curves show the covariance-only estimator, both with 90% confidence-interval error bars. In (a) and (b) the orange curve spikes at 2 interventions and then falls to meet the blue curve at about 0.06 to 0.08 error. In (c) there is only a blue curve, which decreases steadily. Panel (d), labeled Constraints satisfaction, plots the percentage of instances meeting the graphical conditions against the number of interventions. It has three lines for graph densities 0.3 (blue), 0.5 (orange) and 0.7 (green), all rising toward 100%. Legends sit inside the plots. The eye goes first to the orange spikes in (a) and (b).
caption: (a–c) Relative errors of estimated parameters of the OU process versus the number of interventions, and (d) percentage of instances satisfying graphical conditions in Theorem [ref].
abstract: We study the problem of recovering the parameters of a multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process from steady-state observational and interventional data. In many applications, such as large-scale gene perturbation experiments, only stationary "snapshot" measurements are available, making standard stochastic differential equation estimation methods that rely on time-series trajectories inapplicable. We first establish an identifiability result: one intervention per strongly connected component (SCC) of the drift graph suffices to recover all OU process parameters generically up to a global scaling factor. This holds provided that the SCC condensation graph is connected with a single root and certain spectral nondegeneracy assumptions hold. We propose a recursive learning algorithm that orders SCCs topologically and, for each component, isolates its marginal dynamics and solves a linear system derived from the steady-state moment equations, leveraging parameters recovered for upstream components. Building on this theoretical foundation, we propose a regularized least-squares estimator that jointly minimizes residuals of the steady-state mean and covariance equations across observational and interventional data. Experimental results validate our theoretical findings in recovering parameters of the underlying OU process.
